focus: TextureEdgeBleed.ReadPng: locating the PNG across mods' content folders and decoding it
diffSource: since build 16 (2026-10-15T16:52:13Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: ReadPng skips a higher-precedence .dds/.jpg and reads a lower mod's PNG, silently undoing a retexture
findings.detail: ContentFinder returns the texture from the last-loaded mod whose holder has the path, and that holder accepts .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.psd/.dds. Within one mod, a .dds at the same relative path wins over a .png in any of its folders. ReadPng only probes '<path>.png', so when the winning mod ships a .dds or .jpg (e.g. a retexture or texture-optimiser pack loaded after Mounted Weapons) it continues to an earlier mod's PNG. If the canvas size matches, which is usual for a retexture, Apply swaps the original art onto the material. In TextureEdgeBleed.ReadPng's mod loop (around line 123), stop at the first mod (last loaded first) whose folders contain Textures/<texPath> under any accepted extension. Use its PNG only if that mod has no .dds for the path in any folder and the first-folder hit is the .png; otherwise return null so ReadBackGpu reads what is actually loaded.

findings.title: Extension probe is lowercase-only while RimWorld accepts any case
findings.detail: IsAcceptableExtension lowercases the extension, so Shield.PNG loads in game, but Path.Combine("Textures", texPath + ".png") misses it on case-sensitive filesystems (Linux). The result is the GPU readback with the DXT-darkened edges this change set out to avoid. It is a quality fallback, not an error.

findings.title: Core textures always take the GPU path
findings.detail: Core's art is served from Resources and asset bundles after every mod's content holder has been checked, so ReadPng finds no file for a vanilla texPath and ReadBackGpu runs. That is harmless today because shield art is the mod's own. It only matters if a shieldTexPath ever points at vanilla art.

checked: ReadPng mod order (RunningModsListForReading, last loaded first) matches ContentFinder.Get (ContentFinder.cs:20-28)
ReadPng folder order (foldersToLoadDescendingOrder, first hit wins) matches GetAllFilesForMod's first-key-wins dictionary (ModContentPack.cs:390-416)
Returning null on the first found file when LoadImage fails or the size differs is correct: that file is the one RimWorld used, so falling back to the GPU readback is right
LoadImage leaves the decoded texture readable, so GetPixels32 works; the array is copied before the finally block's deferred Destroy
Size check against the loaded texture holds: LoadTextureViaImageConversion never resizes, only changes mip count and format (ModContentLoader.cs:171-216)
PNG and GPU readback both give bottom-up row order, so Bleed's indexing works the same on either path
ReadBackGpu refactor: readable is now destroyed in finally on every path, RenderTexture.active is restored and the temporary RT released
Exceptions from File.ReadAllBytes or LoadImage are caught in Apply and logged once as a warning per material; no per-frame spam because done.Add runs first
MountExtension.MakeShieldGraphic passes the same texPath the Graphic_Single material was loaded from
csproj adds UnityEngine.ImageConversionModule with Private=false, the same pattern as the existing Unity references
Roslyn reports no errors or warnings in the changed files; the changed C# declares no Harmony patches, so verify_patches and precedents do not apply
